name: Wahhabism
scope: The Islamic reform movement founded by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in 18th-century Najd and adopted in 1744 by the Saudi family: strict tawhid (the oneness of God), condemnation of shirk and bidah, reliance on the Quran and Sunna alone within the Hanbali tradition, and the movement's alliance with the Al Saud as it ruled the Saudi states (Britannica 'Wahhabi' and 'Saudi Arabia: The Wahhabi movement'; DeLong-Bas for the Middle East Institute). Texts: the founder's Kitab al-Tawhid and Three Fundamental Principles. It excludes Salafism and Salafi jihadism as wholes, Qutbism and other Islamist movements, and the Saudi state's present policies, which the sources do not tie to the doctrine.

aliases.name: Muwaḥḥidūn
aliases.quote: The term Wahhabi is used primarily by outsiders to distinguish the movement; adherents often refer to themselves as salafī s (“followers of the pious forebears”), a term used by followers of other Islamic reform movements as well. They characterize themselves as muwaḥḥidūn

keyFigures.role: 18th-century Najdi theologian who founded the movement and preached tawhid against shirk
keyFigures.quote: was a theologian and founder of the Wahhābī movement

keyWorks.title: Kitab al-Tawhid
keyWorks.author: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab
keyWorks.quote: he wrote the Kitāb al-tawḥīd (“Book of the Oneness [of God]”), which is the main text for Wahhābī doctrines

summary: Wahhabism is the 18th-century Najdi reform movement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab. It demands strict monotheism (tawhid), condemns saint and tomb veneration as shirk and every source of doctrine beyond the Quran and Sunna as innovation, and aims at an Islamic society built on those two sources. Its fortunes were tied from 1744 to the Al Saud, whose states it served as ruling ideology.

notes: Themes searched: law and religion, authority, jihad and war, interpretation, saints and tombs, the Saudi alliance. Most statements are null: the sources give the doctrine of tawhid and its political alliance, and say little on economy, government, society or world statements. Kitab al-Tawhid itself could not be opened. Where the founder's jihad is concerned, the MEI source says he knew the classical jihad of the sword but centred on tawhid, so war statements stay null.
